text:
I am in the middle of nowhere in Oklahoma. Fortunately, the wind is at my back. It has been 12 days and 11 nights since leaving San Antonito New Mexico. I have many photos to share, but will get to that soon. Many answers to be found in the wilderness. Solitude opens doors. Rural Oklahoma is magnificent. 

Write if you have questions.

I am headed toward Saint Louis, Missouri from Springfield on the Old Route 66, which I connected with in Northeast Oklahoma. This portion of the old road is through of a very hilly section of the Ozark Mountains.  The people of the midwest USA are friendly, kind and generous. 

It requires an amazingly large amount of work to get in shape and stay in shape to be able to make such journeys, even on a regular basis.  The dangers are ever present, requiring a brave and heroic effort just to stay alive.  Contending with the elements of nature is difficult enough, and then there are the loud oversized pickup trucks along with the regular traffic, all due to local commerce, I guess.  I am really not sure why everyone is always running around, going from here to there and back again, but I am sure it has much to do with spending or making money.

Earlier I had the thought to collect all my photos and post them here later, after I settle down somewhere so that I could write a little story about each photo.  After three weeks on the road, often in very desolate yet beautiful situations, I have decided now it is probably easier to simply upload photos as I go along, but to the dismay of some, without commentary. 

It is said a picture can hold a thousand words, and often such words can formulate into questions.  The nature of travel as I do keeps me from writing, rather I focus on reading, listening, navigating, sight-seeing and taking photos.  I have no cellular connection, and the nature of my wifi stops are such that I only will do quick and simple uploads and downloads, and go on my way. 

So for this announcement group, as before, as I move along from one wifi hotspot to the next,  I will dump photos and locations into this space with little or inadequate commentary.  This is not because I have nothing to say, cannot or do not want to share words. To facilitate conversation, you will need to make a comment or ask me a question directly.

Now I have a folder of photos going back three weeks, from the day I began this leg of my fourth cross-country trip, leaving New Mexico, moving slowly through the panhandle of Texas, across Oklahoma and into Missouri, all while trusting in the goodness of the people. 

Very few Americans or otherwise will ever, or have ever, had the opportunity to explore or experience the United States, the land and it's people, in such an independent and intimate way, with such advanced technology, and self-propelled at that.  One might begin to wonder if there would be some sort of special insight, power, or other sublime benefit involved with pursuing such an endeavor.

**Overview of the Mother Road, USA:**

**1. Route 66:**

   - Historic highway in the United States, also known as the "Mother Road" or "Main Street of America."

   - Originally stretching from Chicago, Illinois, to Santa Monica, California.

   - Played a significant role in American culture and history, especially during the early to mid-20th century.
   
**2. History and Significance:**

   - Established in 1926, Route 66 served as a major route for westward migration during the Dust Bowl era and later became a popular road trip route.

   - Known for its unique roadside attractions, diners, motels, and gas stations that sprung up along the route.

   - Symbolizes the spirit of American freedom, exploration, and adventure.
   
**3. Decline and Revival:**

   - Declined in significance after the construction of the Interstate Highway System in the late 1950s and 1960s, leading to bypassing of many small towns along the route.

   - Efforts by preservationists, enthusiasts, and communities have led to a revival of interest in Route 66 tourism and preservation of its historic sites.

   - Designated as a National Scenic Byway and Historic Route 66, preserving its legacy for future generations.

Route 66, also known as the Mother Road, is a historic highway in the USA, stretching from Chicago to Santa Monica. It played a vital role in American history, symbolizing freedom and adventure, though it declined with the advent of the Interstate Highway System, only to be revived through preservation efforts.

The Mother Road, USA, Route 66, represents American freedom and adventure, declining with the Interstate System but experiencing a revival through preservation efforts.
